explain.say: A gemstone is a mineral crystal that is beautiful, hard and rare enough to be cut and polished. Most grow deep underground in hot fluids, cooling magma or rock squeezed by heat and pressure.

faq.a: A ruby is the mineral corundum with a tiny amount of chromium mixed in. The chromium absorbs some colours of light and lets red through. With iron and titanium instead, corundum becomes a blue sapphire.
asks: Are rubies and sapphires the same?

faq.q: How do diamonds get to the surface?
faq.a: Diamonds form about 150 kilometres or more down. Very deep, fast volcanic eruptions carried them up in pipes of rock called kimberlite, so quickly that they did not turn into graphite on the way.
Most gems are crystals that grew slowly from hot water rich in minerals, from cooling magma, or when rocks were changed by heat and pressure. Slow, steady growth makes big clear crystals.
They are rare, beautiful and hard enough to last. Few crystals are big, clear and free of cracks, and it takes skill to cut them so they sparkle.
Diamond is the hardest natural material, 10 on the Mohs scale. Rubies and sapphires come next at 9.

facts: Rubies and sapphires are both the mineral corundum; chromium makes rubies red.
Most diamonds formed more than 150 kilometres below the surface and were brought up in kimberlite eruptions.
Emerald is a green variety of the mineral beryl, coloured by chromium or vanadium.

quiz.say: A ruby and a blue sapphire are the same mineral. What makes them different colours?
quiz.why: Both are corundum; a trace of chromium makes red ruby, while iron and titanium make blue sapphire.

wrong.1: The colour is inside the crystal, not from the lighting.
wrong.2: Cutting adds sparkle but does not change the colour.
